title: The Leap
novel:
Ted stood on his [[rooftop|rooftop]], staring at the city. He had been [[stuck|stick]] for months — no career [[momentum|momentum]], no love life, no [[direction|direction]]. He felt like he was [[standing|stand]] on the edge of something.

"You need to take a [[leap|leap]]," Marshall told him. "A leap of [[faith|faith]]."

Ted was [[hesitant|hesitant]]. "What if I [[fall|fall]]?"

"What if you [[fly|fly]]?" Marshall replied.

Barney was dealing with his own [[leap|leap]]. He had been hiding his feelings for Robin for months. Finally, he [[confessed|confess]] everything to her.

"I like you," Barney said. "I really like you."

Robin was [[stunned|stun]]. She said nothing for a long moment. Then she kissed him.

Ted, inspired by Barney's [[courage|courage]], decided to take his own leap. He [[quit|quit]] his unsatisfying job and [[devoted|devote]] himself fully to Mosbius Designs. He also [[decided|decide]] to start teaching architecture — a dream he had [[abandoned|abandon]] years ago.

"I'm taking the leap," Ted told the gang.

They all gathered on the rooftop as the sun set. The city [[glowed|glow]] below them.

"To new [[beginnings|beginning]]," Lily [[raised|raise]] her glass.

"To leaps of faith," Marshall added.

Barney and Robin held hands. Ted smiled, feeling for the first time in months that he was moving [[forward|forward]].

The season ended with Ted looking at the [[horizon|horizon]], ready for whatever came next.

stick.en: to be unable to move forward

momentum.en: the force that keeps something moving

leap.en: a big jump or a brave risk

fall.en: to drop down from a high place

confess.en: to tell the truth about something hidden

courage.en: the ability to do something frightening

devote.en: to give all your time to something

glow.en: to shine with a warm light

horizon.en: the line where the sky meets the ground
